summary: A solid multi-cluster Kubernetes service discovery design that streams EndpointSlice deltas via per-cluster agents to a global control plane that publishes Envoy xDS, avoiding per-request control-plane dependencies. The explicit bounded-staleness model and deterministic degradation, combined with passive/optional active health signals and strong operational tooling, makes it credible for production with further detail on scaling and deployment topology.
strengths: Clear requirements/targets with pragmatic eventual consistency and bounded staleness to keep the data plane available during outages/partitions
Good operational maturity: backpressure, monotonic xDS versioning, debug/forensics APIs, and multi-signal health integration (readiness + outlier detection + optional probes)
weaknesses: Control-plane scalability and topology are under-specified for the stated peak churn (50k updates/sec) and 2M endpoints: needs concrete sharding/partitioning, multi-region active-active strategy, and failure/consistency behavior across control-plane replicas

Durability/ingestion resilience is optimistic without a queue/log: relying on in-memory hot state + coalescing risks data loss of transient updates and slow rebuilds under large-scale restarts or Kubernetes API throttling; also xDS TTL support/capability constraints need sharper guarantees
